facts.statement: The genus Ledumahadi was described by McPhee and colleagues in 2018.
Ledumahadi fossils were found in the Early Jurassic Elliot Formation in the Free State Province of South Africa.
facts.quote: from the Early Jurassic Elliot Formation in Free State Province, South Africa

facts.statement: The only known species, Ledumahadi mafube, is represented by a single incomplete postcranial skeleton.
facts.quote: The type and only species is L. mafube, known from a singular incomplete postcranial specimen

facts.statement: Ledumahadi was a quadrupedal dinosaur and one of the earliest giant sauropodomorphs.
facts.quote: A quadruped, it was one of the first giant sauropodomorphs

facts.statement: Despite lacking the columnar limbs seen in later giants, Ledumahadi weighed approximately 12 tonnes.
facts.quote: reaching a weight of around 12 tonne, despite not having evolved columnar limbs like its later huge relatives

facts.statement: Ledumahadi possessed very large and robust forelimbs similar to those of its relatives.
facts.quote: It would have had very large, robust forelimbs, consistent with those of its relatives

facts.statement: Unlike later sauropods, Ledumahadi's limbs were naturally flexed rather than purely columnar.
facts.quote: Unlike those of later sauropods, these limbs were naturally flexed, as opposed to being purely columnar

facts.statement: Ledumahadi is considered the largest land animal to have ever lived during the Early Jurassic epoch.
facts.quote: At its time in the Early Jurassic epoch, Ledumahadi is thought to have been the largest land animal that had ever lived

facts.statement: Ledumahadi reached a maximum body mass of around 12 tonnes at the age of 14 years.
facts.quote: At the age of 14 years, L. mafube is estimated to have reached a maximum size of around 12 tonne in body mass

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Ledumahadi in the clade Lessemsauridae within the Sauropodomorpha.
facts.quote: found it to belong to a recently recognised clade of sauropodiformes called Lessemsauridae

facts.statement: Ledumahadi lived between 201.4 and 192.9 million years ago during the Hettangian to Sinemurian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Sinemurian (201.4 to 192.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Ledumahadi is classified as a member of the parent group Sauropodiformes.
Ledumahadi belongs to the dinosaur class Saurischia.
It is debated whether the Triassic-Jurassic extinction event had a significant effect on body size evolution in sauropodomorphs, given that Ledumahadi achieved large size shortly after the event.
facts.quote: Living only a few million years after the Triassic-Jurassic extinction event, it indicates that this event must have either had only a small effect on body size within the sauropodomorph lineage, or may have not affected it at all

rejected.statement: The trackway ichnotaxon Tetrasauropus, estimated to have a hip height of 2 meters, likely belongs to Ledumahadi.
rejected.quote: An ichnotaxon named Tetrasauropus belongs to a sauropodomorph that is estimated to have a hip height of 2 m, meaning that it likely belongs to Ledumahadi
